statements.text: a driver SHOULD use low beams WHEN the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle UNLESS the driver is passing the vehicle

sources.quote: Use your low beams when you are less than 60 metres behind another vehicle unless you are passing it.

statements.note: The rule is about headlight usage, but the condition 'passing it' is in scope for the passing topic. The force is advisory because the source uses a bare imperative without legal markers.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right of the road OR keep in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads UNLESS the driver wants to turn left OR the driver wants to pass another vehicle

sources.quote: Keep to the right of the road or in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads unless you want to turn left or pass another vehicle.

statements.note: The handbook uses 'unless you want to', which is phrased as a desire rather than an intent; the condition is written as 'wants to' to reflect the source wording.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

statements.text: a cyclist MAY use any part of the lane WHEN necessary for safety

sources.quote: However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:

statements.note: The lead sentence ends with a colon and lists reasons; the permission itself is in the lead. The specific reason in m55 is handled in 3.4.4b.

statements.text: a cyclist SHOULD position the bicycle in the lane to discourage passing WHEN the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

sources.quote: However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:
Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

flags.span: too narrow to be shared safely
flags.note: Subjective judgment of lane width and safety.

statements.note: The item is an infinitive phrase explaining the purpose of using the lane. It is treated as advice for the cyclist to discourage passing.

statements.text: a driver MUST maintain a minimum distance of 1 m between the vehicle and the cyclist WHILE passing a cyclist ONLY IF practical IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

sources.quote: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.
(See Diagram 2-11.) Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.
bike lane adjacent to parking bays

flags.note: Subjective judgment of what is practical.

statements.note: The penalty is in m57. The figure m59 is cited as it is referenced in the penalty sentence.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist WHEN possible

sources.quote: Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

flags.note: Subjective judgment of possibility.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn unnecessarily WHILE passing a cyclist BECAUSE it may frighten the cyclist and cause the cyclist to lose control

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control.

flags.note: Subjective judgment of necessity.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly WHILE passing a cyclist WHEN the driver is still some distance away from the cyclist

sources.quote: If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: Vague distance.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD look behind the vehicle AND check the mirrors and blind spots for a passing cyclist WHEN the vehicle is parked on the side of the roadway AND the driver is about to open a door

sources.quote: When parked on the side of the roadway, look behind you and check your mirrors and blind spots for a passing cyclist before opening a door.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in front closely of a large vehicle WHILE passing a large vehicle BECAUSE it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely.

flags.note: Vague degree of closeness.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD allow more room WHILE passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: Vague amount of room.

statements.text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence that may affect the driver's ability to control the vehicle WHILE passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: 6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay well back from farm machinery UNTIL it is [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

flags.note: Vague distance.
Subjective judgment of safety.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass farm machinery UNTIL it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

flags.note: Subjective judgment of safety.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD maintain a [?safe] following distance from a horse-drawn vehicle

sources.quote: Maintain a safe following distance and only pass when it is safe to do so.

flags.note: Subjective judgment of safety.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass a horse-drawn vehicle ONLY IF it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Maintain a safe following distance and only pass when it is safe to do so.

flags.note: Subjective judgment of safety.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD give as much distance between the vehicle and the horse-drawn vehicle as possible WHILE passing a horse-drawn vehicle BECAUSE passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway

sources.quote: When passing, give as much distance between you and them as possible. Passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway.

flags.note: Vague amount of distance.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass any vehicle WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

sources.quote: You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.

statements.text: a driver MUST stop WHEN the driver approaches a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.

statements.note: The condition 'regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front' is a clarification that the rule applies to both directions, not a restriction, so it is not written as a clause.

statements.force_from: text ("must stop" from c1, "stop" imperative in c2)
statements.text: a driver MUST stop at least 20 m from the school bus WHEN the driver is approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing AND the driver is coming from behind the bus

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.

statements.note: The legal force comes from the lead sentence in c1 ('must stop'); c2 specifies the distance for drivers approaching from behind.

statements.force_from: text ("must stop" from c1, "Do not go" imperative in c3)
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT move the vehicle WHEN the driver is stopped for a school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing UNTIL the bus moves OR the lights have stopped flashing

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.

statements.note: The legal force is derived from the context of the mandatory stop in c1; c3 specifies the condition for resuming movement.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO p04:3.4.12a WHEN the driver is on a road with a median strip AND the driver is approaching the school bus from the front

sources.quote: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

statements.note: This exception switches off the duty to stop for drivers approaching from the front on roads with a median strip, as they are not required to stop in this specific configuration.

statements.text: FACT school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus IN Ontario

sources.quote: In Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus.

statements.force_from: context (penalty: "can be fined heavily and get six demerit points")
statements.text: a driver MUST stop WHEN the driver approaches a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing IF VIOLATED a fine AND 6 demerit points

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

statements.note: This statement links the duty in c1 with the penalty in c5. It is distinct from 3.4.12a to explicitly record the penalty clause as required by the method for joining duties and penalties from different passages.

statements.text: DEFINE passing IS a lane change THAT moves past a slower vehicle ALSO CALLED overtaking

sources.quote: Changing your position on the road involves changing lanes or overtaking and passing another vehicle.
Passing is changing lanes to move past a slower vehicle.

statements.text: FACT not all vehicles travel at the same speed, so a driver may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles WHEN the driver is following them

sources.quote: While all public roads have speed limits, not all vehicles travel at the same speed. For example, cyclists, road service vehicles and drivers ahead that are preparing to turn are usually slower than the through traffic. You may want to pass some slow-moving vehicles when you are following them.

statements.note: "May want to" is a possibility, not a permission, so this is a FACT.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD be sure the driver has [?enough space and time] to complete the move [?safely] WHEN the driver is about to change lanes or pass another vehicle

sources.quote: Before beginning, be sure you have enough space and time to complete the move safely.

flags.note: No measure of space or time.
Subjective safety; no observable test.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle UNLESS the driver is [?sure] the driver can do so without danger to the driver or others

sources.quote: Never overtake and pass another vehicle unless you are sure you can do so without danger to yourself or others.

flags.note: Subjective certainty; no observable test.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN the driver is in doubt

sources.quote: If in doubt, do not pass.

flags.note: Subjective state; no observable test.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle

steps.text: use the left-turn signal to show that the driver wants to pass AND check that the way is clear ahead and behind WHEN the driver is about to move into the passing lane
change lanes ONLY IF the driver has signalled
signal that the driver wants to move back into the original lane AND change lanes WHEN the driver can see the entire front of the vehicle being passed in the inside mirror

sources.quote: Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:
how to pass another vehicle

flags.note: Handbook uses 'inside mirror' here and 'rear view mirror' in m43.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR bicycles and small vehicles that may be hidden from view in front of the vehicle being passed AND vehicles that may be turning left in front of the driver AND vehicles or pedestrians entering the road from another road or driveway WHILE passing a vehicle

sources.quote: Watch for bicycles and small vehicles that may be hidden from view in front of the vehicle you are about to pass. Also watch for vehicles that may be turning left in front of you and vehicles or pedestrians entering the road from another road or driveway.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it WHILE passing a vehicle

sources.quote: Be careful not to cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT race AND SHOULD go back to the original lane WHEN the vehicle being passed speeds up

sources.quote: If the vehicle you are passing speeds up, do not race. Go back to your original lane.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

sources.quote: Passing within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover is not permitted.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass left of a centreline WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel

sources.quote: Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass WHEN the driver is approaching the crest of a hill OR the driver is on a curve AND the driver's vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed AND there is not [?enough clear distance] ahead to pass in [?safety]

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass when approaching the crest of a hill or on a curve where your vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed and there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety.

flags.note: No measure of distance.
Subjective safety; no observable test.

statements.text: FACT some roads have special passing or climbing lanes that let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane

sources.quote: Some roads have special passing or climbing lanes. These lanes let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane.
a passing or climbing lane

statements.text: FACT an advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass AND another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane

sources.quote: An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass on the right WHEN the road is multi-lane OR the road is one-way OR the vehicle being passed is a streetcar OR the vehicle being passed is turning left

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left. You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

statements.text: FACT passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left

sources.quote: Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD wait for the vehicle in front to move to the right AND SHOULD NOT suddenly change lanes and pass on the right WHEN the driver is driving in the far-left lane AND there is a slower vehicle in front of the driver

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

statements.text: a driver MAY drive on the right shoulder ONLY IF the driver is passing a vehicle turning left AND the shoulder is paved

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass on the left shoulder

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved. You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass other vehicles with [?extra care] WHEN passing at night

sources.quote: Be very careful when you pass other vehicles at night.

flags.note: No specific hazard named; vague caution.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle at night WHEN the driver has to pass AND the way is clear

steps.text: switch the headlights to low beams WHEN the driver is approaching a vehicle from behind
signal AND check the mirrors and blind spot AND pull out to pass
switch on the high beams WHILE moving alongside the vehicle being passed
pull back into the right-hand lane WHEN the driver can see all of the front of the vehicle being passed in the inside mirror

sources.quote: If you have to pass and the way is clear, follow these steps:
how to pass another vehicle

flags.note: Handbook uses 'rear view mirror' here and 'inside mirror' in m11.

statements.note: Specializes the general passing procedure for night conditions.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR people suddenly opening doors AND doors opened to load and unload WHEN passing parked vehicles

sources.quote: When passing parked vehicles, watch carefully for people suddenly opening doors or for doors opened to load and unload.

statements.text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right UNLESS the driver is driving on a one-way road

sources.quote: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors WHERE passengers are getting off or on WHEN the driver is at a streetcar stop UNLESS an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers at the stop

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.
a vehicle stopped the required two metres behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar

flags.note: Fixed distance in a bare imperative reads like a legal duty, but no legal wording is present.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass [?these areas] at a [?reasonable speed] AND SHOULD be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves WHEN passing a streetcar stop

sources.quote: Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.

flags.note: Refers to streetcar stops mentioned in the previous passage.
No measure of speed.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a moving snow plow

sources.quote: Don't pass moving snow plows under any conditions.

flags.note: Absolute prohibition with no legal wording; stays SHOULD NOT.

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD move to the right AND let faster traffic pass in [?safety] WHEN faster traffic wants to pass the driver

sources.quote: When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety.

flags.note: Subjective safety; no observable test.

statements.text: a driver being passed SHOULD pay attention to oncoming traffic AND SHOULD move closer to the right side of the lane AND SHOULD be prepared to slow down WHEN the driver is being passed on an undivided road AND the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD move into the right-hand lane [?as soon as the driver can] WHEN the driver is in the truck passing lane AND a truck wants to pass the driver

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane. If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

flags.span: as soon as the driver can
flags.note: No measure of time or distance.

statements.text: a truck driver MUST NOT drive in the far-left lane WHEN the road is a high-speed road with three or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane.

flags.note: Hedged scope; not all such roads may have this rule.

statements.text: a driver being passed MUST NOT speed up WHEN another driver is trying to pass the driver

sources.quote: And do not speed up when another driver is trying to pass you. It is unlawful and dangerous.

statements.force_from: imperative ("Do not take", "do so by changing lanes")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped in the same lane WHEN the vehicle pulls to the left or right side of its lane

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers. Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane. If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

statements.note: The instruction 'do so by changing lanes' implies passing in the same lane is prohibited when these vehicles shift position.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a smaller vehicle that is turning left ahead UNTIL the smaller vehicle has moved to the right

sources.quote: Wait for the smaller vehicle to move right before you pass.

flags.note: The heading 'Left turns' implies the vehicle is turning left, but the specific reference to 'smaller' is not defined in the cited text.

statements.note: The condition that the vehicle is turning left is inferred from the heading 'Left turns' and the context of the other passages in the batch.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pull up beside a vehicle turning left WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the vehicle

sources.quote: If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

flags.note: Refers to vehicles turning left, as established by the heading and surrounding context.

statements.note: This is a rule about positioning relative to a turning vehicle, which falls under 'particular road users' or general passing/turning safety. It prevents a dangerous simultaneous maneuver.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay behind a vehicle turning left AND turn WHEN the way is clear WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the vehicle

sources.quote: Stay behind and turn when the way is clear.

flags.note: Subjective judgment of visibility and safety; no objective threshold defined.

statements.note: The condition 'making a left turn behind the vehicle' is inferred from the previous passage c6 in the same paragraph.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT use a left-turn lane to pass

sources.quote: These left-turn lanes are not to be used for passing.

flags.span: not to be used for passing
flags.note: The phrasing 'not to be used' is a strong prohibition, but without explicit legal wording like 'illegal' or 'must not', it is treated as strong advice with unclear legal force.

statements.note: This is a restriction on the use of a specific lane type, fitting section 3.1.4 (Turn lanes).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right AND use the left lanes for passing WHILE driving on a freeway

sources.quote: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit AND SHOULD NOT stay in the far left lane WHILE driving on a multi-lane freeway

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD drive in the right-hand lane WHEN possible WHILE driving on a freeway

sources.quote: Drive in the right-hand lane when possible.

flags.note: No definition of what makes driving in the right-hand lane possible or impossible.

statements.text: a truck driver MUST use the lane to the right of the far left lane for passing WHEN the freeway has three or more lanes in each direction AND the driver is in a large truck

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The rule is stated to apply to 'many' freeways, not all, but no criteria are given for which ones.

statements.note: The prohibition on traveling in the far left lane is combined with the duty to use the lane to the right, as they describe the same lane usage requirement.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD drive in the right lane WHILE driving on a freeway BECAUSE this leaves the other lanes clear for passing

sources.quote: Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.

statements.note: The condition 'in fog' comes from the heading 'Fog › DO'. The action is limited to 'passing' as per the topic scope.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN driving in a whiteout

sources.quote: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.

statements.note: The condition 'in a whiteout' comes from the heading 'Whiteouts › DO'. The action is limited to 'passing' as per the topic scope.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Don't speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly or to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: The second part of the sentence ('to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely') is out of scope for the passing topic.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass other vehicles WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Don't pass other vehicles or speed up suddenly.

flags.note: Stated again in m45 as 'Avoid passing'.

statements.note: The second part of the sentence ('speed up suddenly') is out of scope for the passing topic.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly WHEN driving in a whiteout

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly or speed up to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: The second part of the sentence ('to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely') is out of scope for the passing topic.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass between several snow plows WHEN the snow plows are staggered across the road on a freeway BECAUSE there is not enough room to pass safely AND the ridge of wet snow can throw the vehicle out of control

sources.quote: On freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow. Do not try to pass between them. This is extremely dangerous because there is not enough room to pass safely, and the ridge of wet snow can throw your vehicle out of control.

statements.force_from: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass on the road WHEN a "do not pass" sign is posted for the road

sources.quote: Do not pass on this road.
a regulatory sign

statements.note: The legal force comes from the section introduction for Regulatory signs. The figure is included as the visual reference for the sign.

statements.text: a driver of slow traffic MUST keep right WHEN driving on a multi-lane road AND a "slow traffic keep right" sign is posted

sources.quote: Slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right.
a regulatory sign

statements.note: The sign caption specifies the condition (multi-lane roads) and the duty (keep right). The role is specified as a driver of slow traffic.

statements.force_from: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
statements.text: a driver MUST keep to the right lane WHEN driving on a two-lane section where climbing or passing lanes are provided UNLESS the driver is passing

sources.quote: Keep to the right lane except when passing on two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided.
a regulatory sign

statements.note: The legal force comes from the section introduction for Regulatory signs. The exception for passing is written as an UNLESS clause.

statements.text: FACT the downward lines on a warning sign show the side on which a driver may safely pass

sources.quote: The downward lines show the side on which you may safely pass.

statements.note: This is a description of what the sign indicates, not a direct instruction or prohibition, so it is a FACT.

statements.force_from: context (Temporary condition signs: implied legal force for temporary traffic control)
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a pilot vehicle or pace vehicle WHEN the vehicle is bearing a "do not pass" sign

sources.quote: Do not pass the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bearing this sign.
a temporary condition sign

statements.note: Temporary condition signs are regulatory in nature. The figure is included as the visual reference for the sign.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD recognize a long commercial vehicle on the highway based on rear signage AND anticipate the extended length and limited speed WHEN the driver is preparing to pass the long commercial vehicle on the highway

sources.quote: It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.
Title: Long commercial vehicle (LCV) - Description: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)

statements.note: The phrase 'It is important to' indicates advice. The definition of LCV is not included as a separate statement because the focus here is on the passing behavior.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle WHEN a solid line is at the left of the driver's lane

sources.quote: Pavement markings divide traffic lanes, show turning lanes, mark pedestrian crossings, indicate obstacles and tell you when it is not safe to pass.
A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass. ('A' should not pass.)
vehicles travelling beside a solid yellow line

flags.note: The handbook uses 'unsafe' rather than explicit legal wording like 'illegal' or 'prohibited', but the context of pavement markings indicating safety suggests a legal restriction.

statements.note: The figure m22 illustrates the solid line condition.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass a vehicle WHEN a broken line is at the left of the driver's lane AND the way is clear AND there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely

sources.quote: A broken line at the left of your lane means you may pass if the way is clear. ('A' may pass if there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely.)
vehicles travelling beside broken yellow lines

flags.span: enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely
flags.note: Subjective judgment of distance and safety; no fixed metric for 'enough' lines.

statements.note: The figure m24 illustrates the broken line condition.

statements.text: a driver MUST slow AND carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle

flags.note: No measure of care is given.

statements.note: The legal force comes from the section context, which lists this as an offence. The action is split into two parts joined by AND.

statements.text: a driver MUST move into another lane WHEN passing a stopped emergency vehicle ONLY IF moving is possible IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: Failing to move, where possible, into another lane when passing a stopped emergency vehicle

flags.note: No objective test for when moving is possible.

statements.note: The legal force comes from the section context, which lists this as an offence. The condition 'where possible' is rendered as ONLY IF moving is possible.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT drive a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing

sources.quote: driving a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing

statements.note: The passage is a list item under a sanctions heading, which implies legal force for the behaviour listed.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer cannot accelerate as quickly as a driver without a trailer

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer needs more space than a driver without a trailer BECAUSE the length of the vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached

sources.quote: You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD make sure the driver has [?enough] time and room to complete the pass WHEN the driver is about to pass a vehicle

sources.quote: Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass.

flags.note: No measure of time or space is given.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD allow [?more] room WHEN the driver has passed a vehicle UNTIL the driver moves back to the original lane

sources.quote: Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane.

flags.note: No specific distance is given for how much more room is needed.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT cut back into the original lane [?too soon] WHEN the driver has passed a vehicle BECAUSE it can cause the trailer to sway and make it difficult to control

sources.quote: Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

flags.note: No time or distance threshold is given for when cutting back is too soon.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD signal AND pull over WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass.

statements.text: FACT fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them

sources.quote: Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them.

statements.text: FACT the wall of wind behind a large bus or truck that passes a driver towing a trailer may whip the trailer to the side, pushing it out of control

sources.quote: If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT brake WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by the wind behind a passing large bus or truck

sources.quote: When you experience this, do not brake.

statements.note: The condition 'When you experience this' refers to the trailer being whipped to the side by the wind, as described in the previous sentence.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD [?carefully] steer the vehicle and trailer back into position WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by the wind behind a passing large bus or truck

sources.quote: Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position.

flags.note: No specific steering technique or speed is defined.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer MAY increase speed slightly WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by the wind behind a passing large bus or truck

sources.quote: A slight increase in speed may help.

flags.note: The wording 'may help' is suggestive of advice rather than a legal permission, but 'may' is the only modal available for a non-prohibitive action option.

statements.note: The handbook suggests this as a helpful action, not a strict obligation or permission. 'MAY' is used to represent the option, with an M flag to note the advisory nature.

statements.text: a driver being passed MUST move to the right AND allow the vehicle to pass WHEN the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass the vehicle

sources.quote: When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:
Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.

statements.note: The source is a sample test question. The lead sentence and the selected option are joined to form the complete rule.
